finding.claim: Broken authorization on the ban endpoint. require_admin() denies access by calling abort(403), which raises an HTTPException. ban() wraps the call in `except Exception`, which catches it, logs a warning and carries on to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin user, or a request with no g.user at all (the AttributeError is swallowed too), can ban arbitrary users. unban() calls require_admin() without the try/except, so it is enforced correctly. The two endpoints are inconsistent.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin request (or one with no g.user) to POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an attacker-chosen uid.

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban is exposed with no decorator or before_request auth check.
require_admin(g.user) is called inside a try block.
For a non-admin, require_admin calls abort(403), which raises werkzeug HTTPException (a subclass of Exception).
`except Exception` swallows the 403. The handler only logs a warning at line 19 and does not re-raise or return.
do_ban(uid) runs unconditionally and the endpoint returns ok=True.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is require_admin, which is bypassed by the broad except. There is no before_request hook, login decorator, or other authentication/authorization middleware in the file. unban() does not swallow the exception, so it is not affected. Line 19 also logs the user-controlled g.user name, a minor log-injection and PII concern.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403, but ban() catches it with `except Exception` (admin.py:18) and never re-raises. There is no decorator or before_request hook. unban() at admin.py:26 calls it unguarded, so it is enforced there.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20 the abort(403) from require_admin (raised at line 11, not 10 as the trace says) is swallowed by `except Exception`, so do_ban(uid) runs for any authenticated non-admin; the "no g.user" sub-claim is wrong, since line 19 would raise on a missing g.user and the request would fail before do_ban.

verdict_facts.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403, but the abort is swallowed by `except Exception` at admin.py:18. No decorator or before_request check exists.
verdict_facts.reason: admin.py:17-20 catches the HTTPException raised by abort(403) at admin.py:11 and only logs it, so do_ban(uid) runs for any authenticated non-admin, unlike unban at admin.py:26. The candidate is slightly off in two places: the abort is on line 11, not 10, and a request with no g.user would hit AttributeError again at line 19 and return a 500 without banning. The non-admin bypass is real.
